A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same theory of anytime-constrained equilibria despite the changed title and author list. All 26 pages, including equations, algorithms, and Appendices A–F, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 presents algorithms, theoretical guarantees, proofs, and extensions. Neither the main text nor the appendices report original empirical results.

after.justification: v2 retains the theoretical treatment and appendices without adding experiments, simulations, user studies, or data analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–4 retain the same feasibility construction, reduction to action-constrained games, LP-based backward induction, and cost-rounding approximation. The explanatory edits do not change these procedures.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or tasks for empirical training or evaluation. The revised autonomous-driving motivation does not introduce an evaluated scenario.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods against the proposed algorithms. References to earlier approaches remain theoretical comparisons.

E3.justification: No experimental evaluation protocols or settings appear in either version. The game interaction protocol and mathematical parameter conditions are unchanged.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity experiments, or empirical case studies. The appendix proofs and theoretical extensions are identical.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries are added, removed, or revised. The theoretical findings and quantitative complexity and approximation bounds also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, propositions, lemmas, Theorems 1–4, and corollaries retain their mathematical content. Appendices A–F, containing proofs and extensions, are identical.

C1.justification: Both versions claim feasibility characterization, fixed-parameter tractable equilibrium computation, polynomial-time approximation under cost bounds, and efficient action-constrained game solving. The revised abstract explicitly states P != NP when describing optimality, clarifying the existing NP-hardness rationale without changing the substantive contributions.

C2.justification: The explanations of feasibility, approximation through relaxed budgets, learning applicability, and cost restrictions are retained. Remark 4's explanation of why a cost bound is necessary and Appendix F's extensions are unchanged.

D1.justification: Algorithm pseudocode, LP specifications, rounding rules, and parameter choices are unchanged. Neither version supplies additional implementation, hardware, training-time, or code/data access information.

R1.justification: The same 44 references are retained. Section 1.1 and the introduction's discussion of earlier methods preserve the same research relationships and novelty positioning.

P1.justification: The title changes from Anytime-Constrained Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning to Anytime-Constrained Equilibria in Polynomial Time, and Xiaojin Zhu is removed from the author line. The abstract and opening motivation are revised, with scattered grammatical edits elsewhere; section organization remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The new single-line title and single-author heading shift the first-page layout, and edited passages undergo limited line reflow. Algorithm displays remain unchanged, with no figures or tables added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves clarity through a title focused on equilibrium computation, a more direct explanation of the multi-agent motivation, and explicit P != NP wording in the abstract. These are limited presentation gains; the algorithms, guarantees, proofs, and extensions remain unchanged.
